text.text:
#### Introduction

Look around you. Everything you see has a form: a rock is **solid**, water in a glass is **liquid**, and the air you breathe is a **gas**. These are the three most common states of matter we experience every day.

But are these the only states that exist? And what was happening in the universe before we could detect its very first light, the **Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)**?

In this class, we will explore how matter changes, how it relates to energy, and what this tells us about the beginning of everything.

text.text:
#### A Law of Nature

Scientists have studied these transformations for centuries. One of the most important discoveries was made by **Antoine Lavoisier** in <htdate0>: the **law of conservation of matter**.

This law states that, in nature, **matter is neither created nor destroyed** in any process. When water evaporates, the same amount of water exists -- it simply changed its form.

This understanding helps us realize that everything needed to build what we see today was already available at the very beginning of the universe. Nothing was added or removed along the way.

#### Let Us Think!

We have seen that matter can be solid, liquid, or gas, and that it transforms without being destroyed.

**Are these three states enough to explain everything in the universe?**

#### There Is Something More

The answer is **no**. The three states of matter alone are not enough.

Every state we studied -- solid, liquid, gas -- has **mass**. But nature has another fundamental quantity: **energy**. We need energy to move, to think, to live.

Many scientists have studied the relationship between matter and energy. One of the most famous works was published on <htdate0>, by **Albert Einstein**. In this paper, Einstein showed that matter and energy are two forms of the same thing: **it is possible to transform matter into energy and energy into matter**.

This means that in the very beginning of the universe, before anything visible existed, there was **energy** -- and from that energy, matter was born.

source_menu.text: Penzias, A. A., & Wilson, R. W.

text.text:
#### Putting It All Together

Now we can build a clearer picture of the universe's beginning:

1. More than 13.82 billion years ago, everything in the universe was concentrated in an extremely small space.
2. At that moment, matter and energy were **unified** -- together, inseparable.
3. As the universe expanded, energy began to transform into matter, creating the first particles and eventually everything we see today.
4. The first "picture" we have of this process is the **Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)**, detected in <htdate1> by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson.

Before the CMB, everything was together and concentrated. After that, a separation occurred that allowed stars, planets, galaxies, and ultimately life to form.

#### Conclusion

In this class, we learned that matter exists in different states -- solid, liquid, and gas -- and that these states can transform into one another without destroying anything, as Lavoisier's law tells us.

We also discovered that matter is not alone in nature: **energy** plays a fundamental role. Einstein showed us that matter and energy are two sides of the same coin.

Before the CMB, everything in the universe was concentrated together. Today, matter and energy are spread across Earth, stars, galaxies, and the entire universe.
